title: The Resignation Tadashi Yanai Refused When the Vegetables Failed
dek: In 2004 Uniqlo's parent shut its eighteen-month vegetable venture, and Tadashi Yanai would not let the man who ran it walk away.

story.event: Closing the SKIP vegetable venture and refusing its leader's resignation
story.summary: Fast Retailing, the parent of Uniqlo, began selling low-chemical vegetables under the SKIP brand through its subsidiary FR Foods in November 2002, decided in March 2004 to wind the business up for poor performance, and stopped trading in April 2004. By the account of FR Foods president Osamu Yunoki, who put the losses at 2.6 billion yen, Tadashi Yanai refused his resignation and told him to pay the money back first; Yunoki stayed and later ran the GU clothing chain.
paragraphs: In 2004, as Fast Retailing wound up its vegetable business, the man who had run it went to the company's founder, Tadashi Yanai, and asked to resign. Osamu Yunoki had led SKIP, the group's attempt to sell food, for about eighteen months. He later said he had invited colleagues to join him and then let every one of them down.

Yanai had announced the idea himself. In April 2002, with sales at existing Uniqlo stores falling, he told The Times that the company wanted "to apply the Uniqlo philosophy to food." The plan, as the Japanese press reported that August, was to sell about 100 items online from November, grown by the Nagata method with minimal chemicals and fertiliser, and priced above supermarket levels. Yunoki, a former Itochu trader who had joined Fast Retailing in 1999, became president of a new subsidiary, FR Foods, and SKIP began full operation in November 2002.

In the year to August 2003 the food business took about 0.7 billion yen. The outlook Fast Retailing published late that year still had it opening fourteen more stores, losing about 0.6 billion yen in the year ahead and aiming for profit the year after. In March 2004 the company decided instead to wind it up "on account of poor performance", and SKIP stopped trading in April. Yunoki later put the losses at 2.6 billion yen.

By Yunoki's own account, Yanai would not take the letter. Having lost 2.6 billion yen and learned from it, Yanai asked, did he now simply mean to leave? He should pay the money back first. Yunoki came to see this as a way of keeping him, and said that if he had been shown sympathy, he would certainly have quit.

Fast Retailing went back to clothes. That November, Yanai told shareholders the group would look for new business in "apparel-related areas that fit with UNIQLO's brand." Yunoki stayed, working in marketing and personnel. About four years later he was asked to help rescue GU, the group's struggling budget chain, and refused for three months, he said, because he no longer trusted himself to lead people. He was running it by 2010, and by 2019 a television profile put GU's annual sales above 230 billion yen.

quote.text: When we watch a child trying to walk, we see its countless failures; its successes are but few. If we had to limit our observation within a narrow space of time, the sight would be cruel.
quote.source_title: Sadhana: The Realisation of Life, Project Gutenberg eBook #6842
quote.connection: Tagore was writing about a child, whose falls hurt nobody else. SKIP's fall cost real money and the trust of colleagues who had followed Yunoki into it. Yanai chose to judge him over a longer span than eighteen months; the quote explains that choice without proving it was owed.

reflection: Two people in this story could have ended it badly. Yunoki wanted to leave because he felt he had failed the people who trusted him. Yanai wanted the failure kept, studied and repaid in work rather than walked away from.

When something you built does not work, the instinct may be to take all the blame and step aside. Responsibility can also look like staying: counting what it cost, saying so plainly, and doing the next piece of work better. Yunoki said kindness would have let him go. Sometimes the person who will not release you is doing you a favour, and sometimes rest is the better answer. Only you can tell which it is.
invitation: Think of one thing that did not work this year. Write two sentences, one on what it cost and one on what it taught you, and put the note where you will find it next month.

cross_checks.claim: Fast Retailing began selling food, mainly low-chemical vegetables, under the SKIP brand in November 2002
Yanai publicly backed extending the Uniqlo model into food in 2002
The business was wound up in spring 2004 after about eighteen months
The venture lost more than 2 billion yen (2.6 billion by Yunoki's account)
Yanai refused Yunoki's resignation and told him to pay the money back first
Yunoki was asked to rescue GU in 2008 and was running it by 2010

research_notes: Loss figures differ, so the story gives only Yunoki's own figure and attributes it to him. Yunoki (Hitotsubashi interview, 2018; also the headline of a 2014 Diamond Online interview) put the loss at 2.6 billion yen; Diamond Online (2016) and TV Tokyo (2020) say more than 2 billion yen. Fast Retailing's 2004 annual report books an extraordinary loss of 1.0 billion yen on withdrawal plus 1.8 billion yen of termination payments in fiscal 2004, on top of the unit's operating losses; a Japan Times report of 23 March 2004 (not cited, because it blocks automated readers) gave a planned special loss of 2.8 billion yen. These are different measures (cumulative loss versus one-year charges), not necessarily a contradiction. Duration: the company history gives November 2002 to April 2004 (about seventeen to eighteen months); Yunoki says about a year and a half. Yanai's words exist in three slightly different Japanese retellings ('金を返せ' in Diamond 2014, '借金を返してからにしてください' in Diamond 2016, and Yunoki's fuller version in the Hitotsubashi interview), so the story paraphrases them rather than quoting a translation; the date of the resignation is not given beyond the closure, so the story says 2004. GU dates: TV Tokyo says GU president from 2010; the Hitotsubashi profile lists president of GOV Retailing (GU's operating company) in 2010 and of GU in 2011, so the story says he was running it by 2010. The GU sales figure (238.7 billion yen for 2019) is from TV Tokyo's company profile. Yanai was chairman and CEO from November 2002, with Genichi Tamatsuka as president; the closure decision is attributed to the company. Funding is set to mixed as in the slate: FR Foods was a wholly owned subsidiary financed by the listed parent. The Japanese and Chinese sources load but the verifier cannot match romanised names in them; the two annual reports and the USDA report are PDFs whose text the verifier cannot read, though they load. Japanese passages were read in translation. Tagore wrote Sadhana in English (1913), so no translator is given; he was writing about joy and the problem of evil, and the line is applied here by analogy.
